key_insight: tEHR uses pretrained language semantics to model longitudinal EHRs, with clinical descriptions and two-stage adaptation supporting prediction performance.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support risk prediction from structured patient histories, but the reported results do not establish clinical utility.
method: Represent structured EHR events using natural-language descriptions.
Continue pretraining a causal language model on EHR text streams.
Apply task-specific discriminative fine-tuning with LoRA to encode longitudinal patient histories.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered four MIMIC-IV prediction tasks and CPRD pancreatic cancer prediction at 1–12-month horizons; the Mistral-7B-v0.3 backbone performed strongest overall.
watch_item: The abstract does not report absolute performance, calibration, or prospective validation, limiting assessment of deployment readiness.
paper_title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks
